item.title: Brianna Polen
item.description: ROCKY MOUNT – Brianna Polen, 16, died January 22, 2026 at ECU Health Medical Center, Greenville. Funeral services will be held at 1 p.m. on Wednesday, February 4, 2026 at Word Tabernacle Church, Rocky Mount. Burial will follow at Impact Pointe Cemetery. Matthews Family Mortuary, Rocky Mount, is handling the arrangements.

item.title: Corey Brown
item.description: AHOSKIE – Corey Brown, 48, of Ahoskie died Wednesday, January 28, 2026 at his residence. Funeral services will be held at 2 p.m. on Sunday, February 8, 2026 at Elks National Shrine, Winton. Burial will follow at First Baptist Winton Cemetery. Hertford County Undertakers, Winton, is handling the arrangements.

item.title: J. Carroll Thompson
item.description: J. Carroll Thompson Submitted Photo COLERAIN – Julian Carroll Thompson, age 91, of Elm Grove Rd. in Bertie County, NC, passed away peacefully on February 2, 2026, at his home. Mr. Thompson, who went by “Carroll,” was born on June 19, 1934, to John William (Willie) and Mertie Elizabeth Jernigan Thompson, in the Elm Grove community of Bertie County, NC. item.title: State Board sends letters to voters with unvalidated identification numbers
item.description: RALEIGH - The State Board of Elections is sending letters to more than 241,000 North Carolina voters who provided identification numbers when they registered to vote that did not validate against other government databases. The letters encourage these voters to update their voter records by providing their driver’s license or social security numbers or by ensuring the name on their voter registration matches other official government records. item.title: Northampton County awarded $500,000 State Economic and Infrastructure Development Grant
item.description: GARYSBURG – Northampton County was recently awarded a $500,000 State Economic and Infrastructure Development (SEID) grant by the Southeast Crescent Regional Commission (SCRC). These funds will be used for a lift station replacement in the Town of Garysburg. This project was chosen by the SCRC due to strong alignment with the priorities identified in SCRC’s authorizing statute, Five-Year Strategic Plan, and State Economic Development Plan.
